reason: The tablet is the core of the request desk, but the sponsor app makes its next useful repair unclear.
expectation: The compatibility list should show how to start preparing the tablet for private requests.

effect: The sponsor app is removed and the microphone is physically disconnected, so the tablet is ready for the request-desk fittings.
reaction: The physical disconnection makes the privacy change concrete.
reason: A large button should give people a deliberate way to make requests on the prepared tablet.
expectation: The button will be fitted to the tablet for deliberate requests.

effect: The large button now operates the form's Send control; the microphone remains disconnected.
reaction: The accessible send control is a useful, concrete improvement.
reason: The folded hood should give people more privacy while using the request tablet.
expectation: The hood will fit over the tablet screen to shield requests from nearby viewers.

effect: The tablet now has a privacy hood as well as the large send button.
reaction: The hood addresses a different privacy concern from the disconnected microphone.
reason: The receipt printer is a plausible next fitting for the request desk.
expectation: The printer will connect to the tablet to provide a paper record of a request.

effect: The printer connects to the local controller rather than directly to the tablet, producing a local queue printer with privacy and deletion controls.
reaction: I had expected a direct connection; the separate handling of return details is useful.
reason: The hooded tablet and local queue printer are the prepared parts of the request desk, so I expect them to connect now.
expectation: The tablet will send requests to the local queue and provide receipts.

effect: The tablet connects separately to the local controller, with its outside route blocked and microphone still disconnected.
reaction: I expected it to connect directly to the printer; the controller is the common link instead.
reason: The screen-shielded tablet and local queue printer are now both connected locally, so I will try bringing them together.
expectation: The tablet and printer will form a working private request desk.

effect: The tablet and printer now form a private request desk with receipts and non-digital access.
reaction: The pencil offers a useful alternative to using the tablet.
reason: The remaining goal is optional AI help, so Moth is the natural addition to the desk.

choice.combine: Moth with source display and correction controls

expectation: Moth will provide optional assistance without making AI use mandatory.

effect: Moth's help is opt-in and its proposed wording is shown before sending; the private request desk goal is complete.
reaction: Sal keeping her original wording makes the choice feel genuinely hers.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting Moth as optional help was most worthwhile: people can review its suggestion and retain their own words.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two attempts to connect the printer and tablet directly were repetitive, though the feedback clarified that each needed the controller first.

surprise.text: The printer and tablet each connected to the controller separately before they could form a desk; I had expected a direct connection.

arbitrary.text: The exact connection order was not obvious from the object names, although the compatibility feedback made the required steps clear.

continue.text: I would continue: the practical privacy choices and Sal's response to Moth made me curious how the neighborhood will use what it has built.
